;Arts and culture
*Parts of the [[Ventura Freeway]] in [[Southern California]] is renamed as “President Barack H. Obama Highway” in honor of former President [[Barack Obama]]. [https://www.pasadenastarnews.com/2018/12/20/welcome-to-the-president-barack-h-obama-highway-a-section-of-the-134-freeway-between-glendale-and-pasadena/ (''Pasadena Star News'')] [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/los-angeles-area-freeway-named-barack-obama-59942210 (ABC News)]

;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[International military intervention against ISIL]], [[Syrian Civil War]]
**Reacting to yesterday's announcement by the [[United States]] on the withdrawal of their forces from [[Syria]], [[France]]'s [[Minister of the Armed Forces (France)|Defense Minister]] [[Florence Parly]] says on [[Twitter]] that [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] has not yet been driven out of Syria. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-france/france-says-islamic-state-has-not-been-wiped-from-map-in-syria-idUSKCN1OJ0U6 (Reuters)]
*[[Northern Rakhine State clashes]]
**[[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw|military]] announces it will resume "clearance operations" in [[Rakhine State]] after a recent spike in attacks by unidentified assailants. In the past week, two [[Rakhine people|Rakhine]] fishermen and a teenager were found murdered after they were reported missing, while two [[Barua (Bangladesh)|Maramagyi]] villagers were kidnapped and stabbed but managed to escape their abductors. [https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/2178972/myanmar-forces-resume-clearance-operations-after-two (AFP via ''South China Morning Post'')] [https://www.rfa.org/english/news/myanmar/myanmar-forces-begin-new-clearance-operations-12202018162920.html (Radio Free Asia)]

;Business and economy
*[[Gatwick Airport drone incident]]
**[[Gatwick Airport]] in [[West Sussex]], [[England]], is shut down intermittently since Wednesday night, after drones are seen flying over the airfield. Police believe it is "a deliberate act to disrupt the airport". Hundreds of thousands of passengers are affected. [https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/17310835.gatwick-drone-attack-was-deliberate-act-to-disrupt-airport/ (''The Argus'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/12/20/uk/gatwick-airport-drones-gbr-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Disasters and incidents
*The annual [[Thomson Reuters]] poll among aid agencies shows that the situation in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], with its [[Kivu conflict|war]], [[Poverty in the Democratic Republic of the Congo#Hunger|hunger]] and [[2018 Kivu Ebola outbreak|Ebola outbreak]], is perceived as the most neglected crisis of 2018. The [[Central African Republic]], with its [[Central African Republic Civil War (2012–present)|civil war]], is a close second. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/africa/article/2178847/dr-congo-ravaged-ebola-and-war-most-neglected-crisis-2018 (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[December 2018 British Columbia storms]]
**Severe [[windstorm]]s in [[Vancouver]] and [[Vancouver Island]] damage houses, damage roads, and destroy a 100 year old pier in [[White Rock, British Columbia]]. One person stranded on the pier is rescued by helicopter. Several highways were closed due to trees falling. [https://www.surreynowleader.com/news/white-rock-pier-damaged-by-storm/ (''Surrey Now'')]
* The Mayor of [[Skagway, Alaska]], Monica Carlson, as well as her mother, are killed after being struck by a tour bus in [[Washington, D.C.]] while preparing to visit the [[White House]]. [https://wtop.com/dc/2018/12/2-seriously-injured-in-dc-after-being-struck-by-tour-bus/ (WTOP)]

;Law and crime
*Ten years after the collapse of [[Belgium|Belgian]] financial group [[Fortis (finance)|Fortis]] in the [[financial crisis of 2007–2008]], the prosecutor in [[Brussels]] decides to drop the case against seven former directors. The prosecution argues that it found insufficient evidence that they knowingly misled shareholders with over-optimistic company information. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-crime-belgium-fortis/ten-years-on-belgium-drops-case-against-fortis-ex-directors-idUSKCN1OJ0YK (Reuters)]
*[[Denmark]] passes a law that requires new citizens to shake hands with a Danish official at their [[naturalization]] ceremony. It is widely believed that the law was made to spite potential Muslim immigrants, who usually refuse to shake hands with people of the opposite gender. Several Danish municipalities are openly looking for loopholes in the law. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/12/20/world/europe/denmark-muslims-handshake-law.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Protests break out across [[Sudan]] over rising prices of bread and fuel, resulting in at least eight deaths. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/12/protests-rising-prices-spread-sudan-khartoum-181220132130661.html (Al-Jazeera)]
*[[Abortion in the Republic of Ireland]]
**[[President of Ireland|Irish President]] [[Michael D. Higgins]] signs a bill making [[abortion]] legal in the [[Republic of Ireland]] for the first time. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/health/abortion-becomes-legal-in-ireland-for-first-time-after-bill-signed-by-president-1.3738504 (''Irish Times'')]

;Politics and elections
* [[First cabinet of Donald Trump|Cabinet of Donald Trump]]
**[[U.S. Secretary of Defence]] [[Jim Mattis]] announces his resignation at the end of February 2019. Mattis says that his views are not well "aligned" with those of the [[President of the United States|President]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-mattis/pentagon-chief-mattis-quits-citing-policy-differences-with-trump-idUSKCN1OJ2WR (Reuters)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/12/20/politics/donald-trump-james-mattis-out/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2018 Democratic Republic of the Congo general election]]
**The CENI electoral commission delays the election to 30 December after 80% of the voting machines in the capital were destroyed in a suspected arson last week. [https://www.npr.org/2018/12/20/678598019/derailed-by-fire-and-disarray-congo-delays-presidential-election-again (NPR)]

;Science and technology
*[[Soyuz MS-09]] lands safely on the [[steppe]] in [[Kazakhstan]]. [https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2018/12/soyuz-ms-09-land-unprecedented-orbit-repairs/ (NASASpaceFlight.com)]
*U.S. researchers say that the [[Marburg virus]] has been found for the first time in [[West Africa]]n bats, notably in [[Egyptian fruit bat|Egyptian rousette fruit bat]]s in [[Sierra Leone]]. Marburg is a "cousin" of the [[Ebola virus disease]], which too may be spread by bats. [https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/deadly-ebola-cousin-marburg-found-west-african-bats-n950331 (NBC News)]

;Sports
*Cuba's baseball federation and [[Major League Baseball]] reach a deal that will allow Cuban players to compete in the USA without defecting. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-46626521 (BBC)]
